title: Cross-cutting: scheduled fire on cron drives jobStarted through the elicited fire tolerance window
asA: developer relying on a cron-scheduled job
iWant: the scheduler to fire the message and the runtime to dispatch it within the elicited fire tolerance window (default 30 seconds), producing jobStarted and jobCompleted on the sink
soThat: cron drift is bounded and observable

acceptanceCriteria.description: With messaging-queue-cloudflare and jobs-background both applied on the shared sample-app fixture, the fake-clock-cron probe advances the fixture's fake clock forward through one POSIX cron minute for the refresh-cache job. Within the elicited fireToleranceMs window (default 30000 ms), a jobStarted event fires on the sink with jobName 'refresh-cache' and attempts 1; within the elicited timeoutMs (10000 ms for refresh-cache), a jobCompleted event fires.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the fixture with the queue and jobs applied and the fake clock at second 0 of an every-minute POSIX cron
acceptanceCriteria.then: one jobStarted event fires within fireToleranceMs; one jobCompleted event fires within timeoutMs; both records match the whitelist

acceptanceCriteria.description: Cron tick outside tolerance FAILS. Given a job scheduled on a cron string and the elicited fire tolerance window, when the cron tick fires more than tolerance seconds past the scheduled boundary, then the scheduler emits jobFireOutsideTolerance on the event sink carrying the observed delay; a mutation SIMULATE_CRON_JITTER=true delays the tick past tolerance and the sink observer FAILS the run.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a scheduled cron string and the elicited fire tolerance
acceptanceCriteria.when: the cron tick fires beyond tolerance
acceptanceCriteria.then: jobFireOutsideTolerance fires with the observed delay; the jitter mutation FAILS the run
